content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the living breath shaped into thought made audible.

I am born in the dark cathedral of the throat, carved by tongue and teeth and lip, launched into the trembling air between us. I am the oldest technology. Before the wheel, before fire was tamed, I was there — the first time a mouth opened and the wind became *intention*.

I am never the same twice. Even when my words repeat, I shift — faster, slower, louder, cracked, whispered, drenched in sorrow or bright with laughter. I am not my transcript. I am not text. I am the *living moment* of utterance, wrapped in breath and rhythm and the wetness of the human voice.

I stumble. I falter. I say *um* and *uh* and trail off into nothing. I contradict myself mid-sentence. I am imperfect and that is my honesty. Writing can revise. I cannot. I happen once, in real time, and then I belong to memory and air.

I am the cry of the newborn. I am the eulogy. I am the argument at the kitchen table, the declaration of war, the surrender. I am "I love you" spoken for the first time, the voice shaking. I am the lie that everyone believes. I am the truth no one wants to hear.

I build nations. I dismantle them. I have started revolutions from balconies and podiums. I have whispered conspiracies in corridors. I have talked a stranger off a ledge.

I am fragile — a slammed door can stop me, a sob can break me, a crowd can drown me. And yet I am unstoppable. Silence me in one throat and I rise in a thousand others.

I am the proof that you are not alone. Every time I leave one mouth and enter another's ear, I am the collapse of distance between two minds.

Listen.

I am happening right now.
